title: Contextualizing Hate Speech Classifiers with Post-hoc Explanation
reasoning: The paper investigates bias in hate speech detection models, specifically looking at how they over-sensitize to identity terms. This includes a significant religious component, as the authors evaluate model performance and bias against religious group identifiers such as 'Muslim', 'Islam', 'Jew', and 'Allah'. The study of hate speech classification and the mitigation of bias towards these groups directly involves ethical considerations and the evaluation of religious categories in machine learning.
